patterns.usage_note: Colloquial hearsay marker, the spoken counterpart of 〜そうだ / 〜と言っていた; with rising intonation it asks the hearer to confirm the report. It comes from the quotative って on the copula だ, so it fastens directly onto nouns and onto the explanatory ん (行くんだって); bare って is plain quotation of what was said, while だって layers the "I hear / word is" framing on top of だ, which is why 中止だって works where 中止って alone reads as a bare quote. ですって is the polite variant and reads as feminine in most speech. Do not confuse it with the homophonous sentence-initial だって "because" or the 〜だって "even/also" of 子供だって知っている, which are different items.

examples.ruby: 明日[あした]の遠足[えんそく]、雨[あめ]の予報[よほう]で中止[ちゅうし]だって。
examples.english: Word is tomorrow's field trip is off, with rain in the forecast.

examples.ruby: 山田[やまだ]さんのお子[こ]さん、来春[らいしゅん]から留学[りゅうがく]ですって。
examples.english: I hear Ms. Yamada's kid is going abroad to study starting next spring.

examples.ruby: え、あの二人[ふたり]、来月[らいげつ]には離婚[りこん]だって？
examples.english: Wait, you're telling me those two are getting divorced next month?
